summary: new Date() creates a Date object whose [[DateValue]] is the current UTC time value in milliseconds.

target.notes: Use the same host clock abstraction as Date.now; allocate a fresh JS Date representation.

tests.name: current time is bracketed by Date.now
tests.input: const a=Date.now(); const d=new Date(); const b=Date.now(); console.log(d.getTime()>=a && d.getTime()<=b);
tests.expected_behavior: normally prints true when the system clock does not move backwards during the expression
